dedupe_keys.name: ciw discrete event simulation library for open queueing networks python

description: Ciw is an open-source Python library for discrete event simulation of open queueing networks, widely used to model patient flow through hospitals, emergency departments and ambulance services. It was created by Geraint Palmer at Cardiff University's School of Mathematics and is maintained by a small community of contributors. The library simulates networks of service nodes with multiple customer classes, priority classes, time-dependent arrival and service distributions, server schedules, baulking, reneging, and Type I blocking for networks with limited capacity, and records every event so that waiting times, utilisation and throughput can be computed. It is generic and location-independent: users supply arrival rates, routing probabilities and service times for their own system. Ciw is installed with pip from PyPI (version 3.2.7 at the time of checking), documented on Read the Docs, archived on Zenodo, and released under the MIT licence free of charge. Caveats: it is a code library without a graphical interface, closed networks and spatial movement are not modelled, and building a realistic hospital or ambulance model still needs careful calibration and validation by the user. Simulation uses: capacity planning for emergency departments, wards and critical care, testing surge scenarios and blocking between hospital units, and optimising staffing or bed numbers. Related records: the R simulation package simmer (platform-simmer) offers a comparable process-based engine, and the treat-sim treatment centre model (model-treat-sim-treatment-centre-des) shows a reusable healthcare example built on SimPy.
